absent: Numeric encodings and full combinational semantics of fault status and fault flag constants
Complete memory layouts of fault descriptor, area descriptor, folio, page and table entry structures
Behavior and contracts of middle level installer, table allocators, range setters and cache update helpers
Default value, tuning and concurrency rules for the fault around window size
Swap device lifecycle, swap cache organization, readahead policy and synchronous device criteria
Detailed merge, unmerge and stable node lifecycle beyond the copy decision shown
Device private and device exclusive entry lifecycle and migration to system memory protocol
Userfaultfd arming, write protection and read write tracking interaction with faults
Notifier ordering, address space stability checks and memory counter accounting rules
Arch specific swap restore, cache maintenance and leaf accessors used during installation

findings.text: The finish_fault operation is externally visible and finalizes file backed faults. Callers supply a fault context that already identifies the area, address and resolved storage, and the operation installs a suitable mapping while reporting completion or a fault status.

The do_swap_page operation is externally visible and handles faults on entries that encode swap or special markers. It resolves the entry kind, obtains underlying storage when required, installs a present mapping, and reports major or minor outcome alongside error conditions.

The ksm_might_need_to_copy operation is externally visible and decides whether swap obtained storage may be mapped directly or needs a private replacement. It yields the original folio, a fresh folio, or an error marker for poison.

The can_change_pte_writable predicate is externally visible and reports whether a leaf entry in a given area may gain writability. The decision delegates to separate private and shared policies based on the sharing attribute of the area.

Entry expects a fault context with the target area, fault address, middle level location and either a file page or a private copy already chosen. Table installation and counter updates occur here, with outcomes that include success, fallback to smaller granularity, resource exhaustion, or a request to retry.

Entry expects a captured original entry that is non present, plus the faulting area and address. Handling covers both genuine swap and marker encodings, may wait or perform device migration, and can ask the caller to retry when the current locking mode forbids the required operation.

Write faults against non shared areas use a dedicated copy page while other faults use the file resident page. Non shared mappings undergo an address space stability validation before any table update proceeds.

Mappings respect the current size of the backing file to preserve bus error behavior beyond end of file, with shared memory style mappings exempted from the restriction. When a large folio would cross the size limit, installation degrades to single page granularity.

A larger middle level installation is attempted first when the folio qualifies and no size fallback applies. If that opportunity is absent or declined, handling ensures a leaf table exists by consuming a preallocated table or allocating a new one, treating allocation failure as resource exhaustion.

Leaf installation covers either the full large folio or a single page. Single page is forced when userfaultfd tracking is armed or a size fallback applies. Full coverage additionally requires containment of the folio extent inside both the area and a single leaf table, with the start rewound to the folio origin when granted.

Surrounding faults are enabled only when the area provides a bulk mapping method, userfaultfd has not disabled the optimization, and the configured window exceeds one page. The computed window is aligned to the configured size and clamped to remain within the faulting area and the current leaf table.

Leaf table access is performed under the table lock. A single page installation aborts when the slot changed concurrently, while a multi page installation releases the lock and retries through the fallback path when any slot in the range is no longer empty. Every mapping acquisition pairs with a matching release.

Bulk mapping of neighboring pages runs inside a read side critical section. A leaf table is preallocated beforehand when the middle level slot is empty, with allocation failure reported as resource exhaustion.

Private file write handling moves from validation and anon preparation through preallocation of a private folio and retrieval of file content. On success the file content is copied with tolerance for machine errors, marked current, and finalized into the tables. The file reference is then released, while error paths discard the preallocation.

Shared write handling retrieves file content and then, when the area supports it, temporarily releases the folio to notify the backing store of impending writability. The mapping is finalized and the page is marked dirty on success. Failure paths release the lock and reference without installing.

Non swap encodings embedded in a non present entry are classified by marker kind. Migration markers cause a wait, exclusive markers trigger restoration, private device markers trigger migration to system memory, poison markers report hardware error, generic markers delegate to a dedicated handler, and unrecognized values report bus error.

Swap resolution pins the backing device, prefers a cache resident folio with readahead state update, and otherwise reads from the device using a synchronous or readahead path according to device capability. Successful device reads count as major faults, while unchanged entries with failed allocation report resource exhaustion.

Swap installation acquires the folio lock with retry support and revalidates that the folio still matches the original swap identity and carries no poison. The table lock is then held to confirm the entry is unchanged and the folio is current. Sanity checks forbid unexpected exclusive or filesystem flags at this point.

Full folio swap installation requires that the folio extent lies within the area and a single middle level range and that all covered slots carry contiguous swap offsets. Exclusivity follows the entry marker except for merged pages and fresh copies, with an exception that clears exclusivity for pages under writeback on devices without stable writes.

New present entries inherit baseline protection from the area and preserve soft dirty and userfaultfd indications from the original entry. Entries that must trap for read write tracking are left inaccessible, and writability plus dirtiness are granted only to exclusive pages in writable areas without conflicting markers.

Concurrent table changes, fork sharing of swap entries, device removal, swap reuse, writeback, migration and poison can invalidate state observed before locking. The code rechecks identity under lock and prefers reporting resource exhaustion, bus error, hardware poison or retry over installing a stale or unsafe mapping.
The base swap identity for a folio is derived by rounding the faulting subpage swap value down to the folio span, so all subpages of the same folio share one aligned origin.

Direct mapping is allowed for large folios, for stable merged pages while unmerging is disabled, for folios without anon ownership, and for linear pages still attached to the same anon hierarchy as the faulting area. Remaining cases allocate and charge a fresh folio, copy with machine error tolerance, and mark the result dirty, current and locked.

Sameness of a previously mapped leaf entry is tested under the table spinlock only where the entry is wider than a machine word on preemptible or multiprocessor builds. The mapping is always released and cleared, with the result indicating whether the entry was unchanged.

Exclusive marker removal takes a folio reference and lock with retry support, brackets the table update with a single page invalidation notification, and restores a present entry only when the original entry is unchanged. Restoration preserves soft dirty and userfaultfd indications, honors read write tracking protection, conditionally grants writability per area policy, and updates the address cache.
Writability policy is selected by the sharing attribute of the area, applying the private rule to non shared areas and the shared rule to shared areas.
